No source file imports another package's private paths.
Composition root injects side-effectful services.
Domain/schema packages reject imports of React, browser globals, SDKs, Node runtime libraries and provider objects.
Core production entry points do not import advanced extension packages.
Use strict TypeScript with noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes.

Select exact supported React/TypeScript/Vite/runtime versions during implementation, pin a lockfile and record them under G06; this spec does not claim versions have already been installed or reviewed.
CI runs frozen install, import-boundary check, typecheck, unit tests, build and static browser smoke tests.
Vite emits relative asset paths.
Use hash-based client routes so static deep links do not require server rewrites; public URLs never contain vault secrets, payment instructions or transaction signing payloads.
A URL/QR can prefill validated public data but cannot execute a wallet command.
Unknown routes show a safe recovery/navigation page.
Browser startup begins locked/watch-only, validates release/network configuration, initializes routing policy, then creates services; no wallet connect or permission prompt occurs automatically.
Production has no service worker in the first core release.
Offline read-only behavior means the already loaded app may show explicitly stale authenticated state; it does not promise offline installation or fresh chain state.
Enabling a service worker later requires cache/update/secret-retention specifications and review.
No source maps containing private development fixtures or credentials ship in the public artifact.
Static configuration contains only public values.
The application composition root owns a disposable service container: storage, backup, identities, transport, wallets, chain adapters, relay and extension registry.
A single `start(publicConfig): Promise<CoreResult<AppServices>>` validates config before services with network authority initialize.
`dispose(): Promise<void>` aborts jobs, locks keys, closes sockets/IDB, invalidates handles and subscriptions.
React components receive view models and explicit commands, not keys/providers.
Routes are home, offers, trade/<opaque local ID>, recovery and settings; a trade route resolves through validated local bindings and cannot treat a URL contract address as an approved deployment.
Only purpose-bound record commands cross the Worker boundary.
There is no generic read, list or commit of records.
**Commands.** The three runtime operations are `saveTermsReview`, `listTermsReviews` and `deleteTermsReview`.
- Each command names `profileId`.
The Worker refuses with `LOCKED` unless that profile is the open selection.
- The document accepts a reply only if the same profile handle is still open.
- The commands act only on `trade` records whose payload is exactly `p2p-offramp/saved-terms-review/v1` ([saved-review.ts](../../../packages/schemas/src/saved-review.ts)).
- Any other `trade` record is reported only as a `skipped` count.
These commands never return, replace or delete it.
**What is stored.**
- The payload holds the original terms-file bytes (1 B to 64 KiB, the domain review bound) and the source label (`file` or `synthetic-sample`).
- Nothing derived is stored.
Every load re-runs the domain terms review against the registry in the running build.
- Saved bytes that no longer pass review are listed by record id with their rejection code, so the user can delete them.
They are never displayed as a review.
**Bounds, retry and ids.**
- A profile holds at most 8 saved reviews.
A ninth save is refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; nothing is evicted.
- Saving is idempotent per (source, bytes).
A retry after an uncertain reply, for example a lock during the commit, stores at most one copy.
- Record ids are random 128-bit values.
An id that collides with any existing record is refused with `CONFLICT`, never overwritten.
**Lock, unlock and profile switch.**
- The UI keeps an opaque `selectionScope()` counter that changes on every lock, unlock or profile switch.
- When it changes, the review controller drops reviews loaded from the profile and discards any saved-review result still in flight.
**Activity pings.** A trusted-activity ping pending from the same click no longer makes that click's command `BUSY`.
Only one public command runs at a time.
**Tests.**
- `packages/schemas/test/saved-review.test.mjs`
- `apps/web/test/saved-reviews-worker.test.mjs` (real encrypted vault)
- `apps/web/test/saved-reviews-controller.test.mjs`
- `scripts/test-saved-reviews-browser.mjs` (emitted demo build in Chromium)
Boundary validation failure produces a fixed error page with local recovery/export where available.
Missing Web Crypto/IDB secure context disables encrypted private operations; do not fall back to plaintext persistence.
Missing chain/provider capability yields explicit unsupported state.
Assets and optional modules failing to load must not reset user data.
Static hosting avoids server custody but does not make delivered JavaScript trustworthy.
Host/build compromise, malicious dependencies, XSS, misleading wallet requests and origin changes remain risks.
Apply G04 CSP/content boundaries and signed release/update verification.
Secrets in build env become public if embedded; CI must scan artifacts and use explicit public-config allowlists.
Relative paths and hash routes support multiple base paths but do not solve IndexedDB isolation across origins; G03 file recovery is required.
Boundary tests intentionally import a provider or React into domain and must fail.
Build a core-only artifact and inspect its dependency graph for advanced modules/server code.
Browser tests cover root and nested-path static hosts, hash deep-link reload, IPFS-style base paths, missing chunks, denied storage, offline recovery, locked startup and disposal during async work.
Assert zero automatic wallet prompts and no private data in URL/localStorage/cache.
Accessibility and responsive/mobile matrices remain separate required specs.

Sources: [Vite static deployment](https://vite.dev/guide/static-deploy), [TypeScript compiler options](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/), [G04 content policy](../../../05_ADVANCED_PRIVACY_INFRASTRUCTURE/feature_5.12_browser_security/module_5.12.1_content_boundary/spec-client-content-security-policy.md).
Framework versions and browser support need evaluated implementation evidence.
Keep chain observations, relay advertisements, wallet consent, local intent and manual fiat claims separate.
No optimistic reducer transition creates spendable value or proves fiat receipt.
Finality is the adapter's observed chain policy, not a locally guaranteed economic fact.
Amounts remain canonical unsigned decimal base-unit strings supplied by the escrow/asset contract; never JS floating point.
`height` is a decimal string, not a Number cast.
Relay order state and local messaging state are separate stores and cannot overwrite `chain`.
Persist minimal recovery references in G02; do not persist a UI success flag as authoritative money state.
The reducer is pure and never performs I/O or calls wallet methods.
Per binding and generation, the reconciliation coordinator assigns increasing requestSequence before an RPC request.
Only the latest-issued reconciliation response may update the current chain view; late older responses are discarded.
A new reconciliation starts at loading/stale and requires chain identity/deployment validation.
Sequence order is local observation order, not a blockchain fork-choice algorithm.
A chain state transition follows the deployed contract: absent -> funded -> released/refunded.
An observation contradicting a previous anchor/state is `reorged` until a fresh canonical read resolves it; do not hide contradictory evidence behind last-writer-wins.
Confirmations can regress and finalized observations can be contradicted by an untrusted RPC.
Any such conflict blocks economic actions rather than assuming monotonic truth.
Economic preflight rechecks the current escrow from the configured adapter immediately before preparation and again checks wallet generation before signing.
Clock-based freshness is display-only; a maximum 30-second UI age marks the view stale, but a fresh label never substitutes for preflight.
User fiat claims alter only fiatClaim.
Buyer-paid messaging cannot release escrow.
Seller-attests-received enables a release request only if the seller is the connected account and the adapter verifies funded/predeadline state.
Unknown chain state disables funding/release/refund preparation; offline views and encrypted export remain available.
The dispatcher validates kind-specific payloads before invoking the reducer.
Wallet account/network events increase walletGeneration and cancel stale preparations; journal entries remain bound to their original account/network.
A local vault conflict requires reload/unlock; it does not merge economic commands.
Multi-tab writes use G02 compare-and-swap.
A single per-profile coordinator serializes same-trade economic intents across tabs using persisted unresolved G12 entries; a BroadcastChannel notification is a UI optimization, never a lock.
Replay/out-of-order events could display paid/released without a valid chain observation; source isolation and reconciliation prevent that promotion.
A malicious RPC can still fabricate current state, so registry checks and disagreement handling remain explicit trust assumptions.
UI optimistic updates must use pending labels and never prompt fiat payment before funding finality.
Cross-tab contention must not create two wallet submissions; journal reservation is committed before a wallet send-capable call.
Restored backups are stale by definition and start with chainHealth loading.
Property-test random duplicates, out-of-order events and wallet generation changes: reducers remain deterministic and pure, and relay/fiat events never finalize escrow.

Test an older refresh completing after a newer one, exact age boundary, release/refund contradictory anchors, reorged funding, cold-start restore, account/network switches and two-tab same-trade submission attempts.
Both EVM and Solana finality adapter fixtures must pass.
requirements.scopeNote: Existing local/native EVM or display-only primitives are related evidence only; this source clause requires the still-open actual browser/live/native-family integration.

requirements.text: Sources: [system context](../module_0.4.1_system_boundaries/spec-system-context-contract.md), [G02 vault](../../../05_ADVANCED_PRIVACY_INFRASTRUCTURE/feature_5.7_local_data_isolation/module_5.7.2_indexeddb_vault/spec-indexeddb-encrypted-records.md), [transaction journal](../../../01_P2P_SHIELDED_OFFRAMP_ENGINE/feature_1.7_transaction_recovery/module_1.7.1_transaction_journal/spec-transaction-lifecycle-journal.md).
Evolve record schemas without corrupting existing vaults or changing the authority of funded trades.
G02 encryption envelope v1 remains fixed.
Different encryption/KDF formats require a separately versioned recovery implementation, never opportunistic reinterpretation.
Migration registry is reviewed bundled code, keyed by kind/fromVersion.
Every produced payload is validated by the destination schema.
Unknown record kinds are rejected by G02; known kinds with future consumer schemas remain opaque/read-only and exportable.
No migration may invoke wallet/RPC/relay, infer a new deployment, alter token decimals, drop a pending intent or retire an identity as a side effect.
Unlock/authenticate G02 and read a consistent snapshot at `(profileId,keyId,revision)`.
Reject mutation if any record's schema is newer than this client supports; preserve original vault for encrypted export.
Build the full sequential migration plan before changes.
Require contiguous version steps, acyclic registry, no skipped versions and schema validation before/after every step.
Cap at 64 steps per record and G02's existing record/payload/snapshot limits.
A missing path returns UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.
Execute transformations on defensive copies outside IDB transactions.
Preserve record IDs, kind and semantic chain/account/deployment/amount/terms bindings.
Payload length may change only within G02 limits.
If any record fails validation, discard the complete candidate snapshot; never partially migrate.
For at most 256 changed records, use one G02 commit with the original expectedRevision.
G02 CAS prevents another tab from overwriting the source concurrently.
After success verify count and authenticated readback; errors keep the source snapshot or the complete new revision.
Larger migrations or changes requiring fresh keys use a new-profile staged migration through G03's authenticated import pipeline, with fresh profile/key/DEK and revision zero.
Invoke G03 InternalMigrationResealer.migrateAndReseal with the live source session, expected key/revision and reviewed bundled migrationId.
That separate internal interface resolves the transform; ordinary public BackupService.restore remains byte-preserving and has no transform parameter.
Retain the old profile and select the new profile only after durable success.
No persistent active-profile pointer is added by this spec.
On interruption restart from persisted state and the same deterministic registry; never replay already-applied steps.
Downgrade clients may export ciphertext but MUST refuse writes to unknown/future records.
No automatic destructive reset, deleteDatabase or same-profile envelope-format overwrite is allowed.
Apply rechecks source identity/revision and recomputes the plan rather than trusting supplied plan contents.

`CONFLICT` requires fresh unlock/replan, `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` offers encrypted export, `INVALID_INPUT` identifies a fixed schema code without record contents, and `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` requests archive/export.
Cancellation follows G02/G03 durable-outcome rules.
The destination passphrase is required only for a new-profile migration and never persisted.
G03 remains callable without transforms for ordinary backup restore.
Malicious imported data can exploit migration parsers or trigger data loss.
Bound every step, reject unknown fields/prototype keys in consumer schemas and run pure transformations without network authority.
A valid encrypted backup can still contain hostile user payloads; authenticated does not mean semantically trusted.
Same-version incompatible schema changes are prohibited.
Two-tab upgrade races must conflict, not lose pending intent history.
In-place broad overwrite or backup deletion can destroy recovery; source profiles are retained.
Test each adjacent migration with fixed before/after fixtures, already-upgraded idempotence, missing/cyclic steps, future versions, malformed payloads and all size bounds.
Inject failure on every record and verify no partial write.
Test 256 and 257 changed records, concurrent source revision changes during transform, app crash/cancel/quota before and after commit, and older-client write refusal.
Assert all trade bindings, unresolved journal IDs and messaging identity bytes survive.

Sources: [G02 vault](../../../05_ADVANCED_PRIVACY_INFRASTRUCTURE/feature_5.7_local_data_isolation/module_5.7.2_indexeddb_vault/spec-indexeddb-encrypted-records.md), [G03 recovery](../../../05_ADVANCED_PRIVACY_INFRASTRUCTURE/feature_5.7_local_data_isolation/module_5.7.2_indexeddb_vault/spec-encrypted-backup-recovery.md), [IndexedDB](https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB/).
Give callers stable recovery behavior without leaking raw provider errors or repeating uncertain economic actions.
Distinguish locally rejected preparation, read failure and possible broadcast.
Existing G02 Result/VaultError shapes remain compatible and are normalized at the application boundary.
Adapters expose CoreResult and translate foreign thrown exceptions into these fixed errors.
G02 retains its documented Result and maps at the coordinator.
Telemetry is off by default; correlation IDs are not global/device/session identities and are never appended to external protocol messages.
Only policy-authorized idempotent reads are eligible for automatic retry.
Use at most three total attempts, each with a 10-second timeout, with full-jitter delays uniformly chosen in [0,500] ms then [0,1000] ms; the overall operation budget is 35 seconds including delays.
Cancellation and G05 generation invalidation stop new attempts immediately.
Resource caps remain those of the requested adapter; read retry never enlarges buffers or resets overall deadlines.
`INVALID_INPUT`, `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`, `UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER`, `WRONG_CHAIN`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `USER_REJECTED`, `LOCKED`, `CONFLICT`, `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`, `EXPIRED` are not automatically retried.
`TIMEOUT`/`UNAVAILABLE` are retryable only for reads.
`CANCELLED` is never retried.
A publish, wallet signing request, transaction submission, token approval, release or refund has zero automatic resubmission attempts.
`BROADCAST_UNKNOWN` always maps to reconcile, never retry.
Relay publication retry requires its separately specified native event-ID idempotency policy; it is not assumed safe by this generic wrapper.
A provider HTTP 429/503 may inform a longer user-visible wait but cannot override the 35-second budget.
Parse Retry-After only as bounded provider data; no sleep after cancellation.
Uncertain outcomes survive app restart in G12.
Inject clocks/randomness for tests only.
Each timed-out attempt aborts and awaits its wrapper completion before another starts; adapters that cannot cancel must have stale outputs discarded and bounded concurrency.

Errors map as follows: bad input -> edit-input; locked -> unlock; wrong chain/provider -> reconnect/change-provider; conflict -> reload; integrity failure -> change-provider and no automatic retry; uncertain broadcast -> reconcile; unsupported format -> export/recovery; cancelled/user rejected -> none.
No exception message or stack goes into public errors.
Unknown provider errors before any send become UNAVAILABLE; any failure after a send-capable call begins is classified conservatively through G12 rather than presumed unsent.
Raw JSON-RPC and wallet exceptions can contain signed requests, addresses, URLs with credentials and user text.
Normalize and discard them at boundaries; debug mode cannot turn on secret-bearing logs in release builds.
Retry storms amplify outages and linkability, so enforce attempt/deadline limits and no parallel retries.
False-negative submission errors can duplicate deposits or expose unnecessary allowances; reconcile instead.
A fixed message code is not proof of the server's honesty.
Use fake clocks and deterministic jitter to assert exactly three attempts at most, 35-second deadline, abort before/during/backoff, no overlap, and no retry for all nonretryable codes.
Test provider 429 with negative/huge/malformed Retry-After, callbacks arriving after timeout, and network generation changes.
For every wallet/economic operation assert one invocation even on error; assert BROADCAST_UNKNOWN retains durable journal references.
Secret fixtures in arbitrary nested errors must not appear in UI/log output.
Sources: [DOM AbortSignal](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#abortsignal), [EIP-1193 errors](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1193).
Allow later privacy/evidence/courier/arbitration modules without making them hidden core dependencies or granting authority over existing funded trades.
Extensions are reviewed bundled code, not arbitrary remotely loaded plugins.
Context exposes validated read/proposal methods, not raw spending keys, global wallet/provider references, storage DEKs or direct network clients.
Module-specific evidence/intents have exact schemas registered before initialization; arbitrary JSON proposal data is rejected.
A build-time registry enumerates supported manifests.
Runtime does not fetch executable code or import an ad-supplied URL.
Core validates manifest format/version, exact coreApiVersion, capability names, limits and schema hashes.
Missing/unsupported modules remain `unsupported` without affecting core trade exits.
Before offer acceptance, both parties select the exact extension ID/protocolVersion/capability/schema hash set, sorted lexicographically by ID with no duplicates.
That immutable set is included in the canonical agreed terms and terms commitment under the terms spec.
Basic trades use an empty set.
The funding preflight rejects unrecognized or unavailable required capabilities.
Optional display-only capabilities cannot become required settlement conditions after funding.
Initialize is once per active generation; failure disables that instance and aborts its jobs.
Dispose revokes context handles, aborts network/workers via scoped service capabilities and removes subscriptions.
A disposed instance cannot publish late results.
No extension directly changes escrow or core reducer authority.
An arbitration module requires a separately deployed opted-in escrow version; loading it in UI cannot give arbitrators rights in a basic escrow.
Basic release/refund/recovery remains available when all optional modules are absent.
Registry APIs are `resolve(id, protocolVersion): ExtensionInstance | null`, `negotiate(manifests): CoreResult<NegotiatedCapabilitySet>`, and `disposeAll(): Promise<void>`.
`NegotiatedCapabilitySet` is the immutable sorted array of validated manifest identity/version/capability/schemaHash fields used in terms, with at most 16 modules.
Unsupported version/name/hash returns UNSUPPORTED_VERSION or UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER before signing.
Runtime adapter/network failures return the module-specific error and preserve core exits.
G13 governs error redaction; economic proposals still require core checks, durable G12 reservation and user wallet consent.
A malicious bundled extension has same-origin JavaScript privileges; capability interfaces are architectural discipline, not a secure JS sandbox.
Treat extension selection as a dependency/security review decision under G06.
Downgrade attacks are prevented by immutable term commitments and unsupported-version refusal.
A plugin cannot assert a proof/score is sufficient for settlement without the actual opted-in deployed contract enforcing it.
Provider outage may block that opted-in feature but must never rewrite existing contract terms or trigger a hidden alternate adjudicator.
Build a core-only artifact with advanced packages physically absent; complete basic discover, fund, chat, manual release/refund and recovery.
Test duplicate/oversized manifests, unknown API versions, changed schema hashes, unsupported requirements, empty/basic negotiation and immutable funded terms.
Dispose during init/network/worker work and assert no late side effects.
A fake extension proposal must not bypass signer/network/deployment/state checks.

Sources: [development roadmap](../../../DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md), [system authority](../module_0.4.1_system_boundaries/spec-system-context-contract.md), [G06 dependency policy](../../feature_0.9_security_assurance/module_0.9.1_dependency_provenance/spec-cryptographic-dependency-policy.md).
Require traceable evidence for release claims.
A checked document heading, generated inventory or green link checker is not product acceptance.
Gates attach to exact source, dependency and deployed artifact identities.

GateRecord: `{id,milestone,requirementIds,specDigests,sourceCommit,artifactDigests,testCases,targetMatrix,reportDigests,reviewer,decision,decidedAt,expiresOnChange}`. decision is pending, failed or passed; waived is prohibited for mandatory critical/high security blockers.
Each test result is pass/fail/unsupported/not-run with logs and environment.
Unsupported is acceptable only for optional advertised-as-unavailable features, never a mandatory chain/recovery path.
M0: primitive known-answer/tamper tests, separate key lifecycle, G02 authenticated persistence, G03 fresh-key restore on new origin, G04 hostile content and G05 strict-route refusal.
M1: reproducible static build, migrations/downgrade rejection, chain/account-change cancellation, uncertain broadcast reconciliation, core-only module exclusion and G15 trust/bootstrap checks.
M2A: EVM native/allowlisted ERC-20 release/refund and adversarial cases.
M2B: Solana native/allowlisted SPL parity with signer/account/program validation.
requirements.scopeNote: Existing local/native EVM or display-only primitives are related evidence only; this source clause requires the still-open actual browser/live/native-family integration.

requirements.text: M2C: full G24 browser/device matrix, independent recovery, G25 rollback, G26 incident drill, WCAG 2.2 AA assessment, reviewed safety translations, license/SBOM evidence and independent security review.
M3–M6 add capability-specific circuit/privacy/hardware/arbitration evidence and must rerun basic trade regression.
Any unresolved critical/high finding makes decision failed; all risk acceptances for lesser findings identify owner and rationale.
A gate is passed only when every mandatory row has applicable evidence and named review of its scope/limitations.
`evaluateGate(records,releaseCandidate)` verifies artifact/spec identity and reports missing, stale or failing evidence, without auto-approving semantic review.
Store artifacts append-only with hashes; superseding results link prior failures rather than erasing them.
Review decisions distinguish designer, implementer and independent reviewer roles.
GATE_INCOMPLETE, TARGET_UNTESTED, REVIEW_SCOPE_MISMATCH and STALE_EVIDENCE block promotion.
Browser emulation alone cannot mark physical mobile-wallet/device cases passed.
Flaky tests need investigated causes; rerunning until green without explanation is not acceptance.
Changed dependencies, compiler flags, deployment or cryptographic artifacts invalidate relevant rows.
Acceptance report must show totals and every not-run/unsupported target, not just aggregate pass percentage.
Include negative tests for wrong origin/network, corrupted backup, expired terms, seller withholding disclosure and expiry equality.
Verify that build/deployment cannot promote with a mandatory pending row.
Current status is design baseline with implementation and independent review pending.

Primary references (exact implementation revisions must be pinned in the evidence record): [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/); [GitHub Actions security](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions).
Turn the authoritative DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP milestone order into explicit implementation prerequisites.
Specification expansion is a design baseline; it is not completion of any milestone or permission to use real funds.
WorkItem schema: `{id,milestone,specPaths,specDigests,predecessors,owner,reviewer,status,evidenceDigests,blockingFindings}`.
Status: proposed → specified → implementing → evidence-ready → independently-reviewed → accepted; blocked is a reason-bearing condition, not an accepted state.
A spec change invalidates affected evidence by digest.
No custodial-ledger branch database becomes authority for noncustodial escrows.
React/TypeScript/Vite and external wallets are the initial core architecture.
Topologically order mandatory work: M0 G06 provenance → G01 key separation → G02 vault → G03 fresh-key backup restore → G04 content and G05 transport enforcement.
M1 consumes M0: static shell, state authority/migrations, wallet/network adapters, transaction journal, optional-module interface and G15 release trust.
M2A consumes M1: canonical immutable terms → EVM escrow/token validation → discovery/chat → complete UI and recovery.
M2B implements separate Solana/SPL parity with equivalent economic properties.
M2C requires both and G24 QA/G25 deployment/G26 incident rehearsals; remove every advanced package and repeat core flow.
M3 optional privacy; M4 optional fiat evidence; M5 physical coordination; M6 opt-in arbitration.
Later optional modules depend on core extension contracts and their own primitives, not availability of every previous service.
A research prototype cannot satisfy a funds-enabled predecessor gate.
`canStart(item,ledger)` checks accepted mandatory predecessor records and unresolved blocking decisions.
`canPromote(milestone)` additionally checks the acceptance matrix and exact source/artifact evidence.
Implementation starts in independently reviewable slices with testable interfaces.
Unsupported optional capabilities are explicit descriptors and cannot appear as enabled in terms.
Parallel work, if performed later, may use frozen contracts but cannot mark integration accepted until combined evidence passes.
DEPENDENCY_CYCLE, PREDECESSOR_UNACCEPTED, SPEC_DRIFT and EVIDENCE_MISSING block acceptance.
Missing prover/provider must not block basic M2C or result in silent false support.
Scope reduction cannot rename M2A “full Phase 2”; Solana parity remains required.
Critical/high findings block release; integration failures reopen dependent items.
Validate DAG cycles and orphan dependencies, map each roadmap deliverable to an owner/evidence record, and rehearse invalidation after key/schema/terms changes.
Manual review checks semantic completeness rather than counting headings.
Required next gates are implementation tests, browser interoperability, chain test-network evidence, independent security review and release rehearsal; none is declared passed here.
Primary references (exact implementation revisions must be pinned in the evidence record): [Vite guide](https://vite.dev/guide/); [Web Cryptography API](https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/).
Repository DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md is authoritative for scope/order.
Enumerate exactly what maintainers can change and prevent off-chain administration from becoming undisclosed custody.
Core v1 escrow is immutable with no admin withdraw, pause-release/refund, confiscation, arbitrary call, operator release or upgrade authority.
Publishing software is distinct from controlling already-deployed escrow.
| Actor | Allowed authority | Forbidden authority |
| Repository maintainer | Reviewed source changes and new version proposals | Moving users' funds or rewriting funded terms |
| Release signer | Sign reviewed artifact/registry version | Changing a deployed immutable escrow |
| Registry curator | Approve new deployment/assets; deprecate new use | Reassign an existing funded trade |
| Relay/directory operator | Host/distribute/censor messages | Authorize escrow release from message status |
| Seller | Release bound crypto before deadline | Change buyer/asset/amount after funding |
| Any refund trigger | Invoke eligible timeout refund | Change refund destination from seller |
| Optional arbiter/courier | Only explicitly opted-in separately deployed terms | Authority over basic escrow |
Release trust roots belong to G15; app binaries may be replaced by hosting operators, so users must verify independently trusted artifacts.
No on-chain governance contract is introduced by this administrative model.
A new deployment has a new registry identity and immutable code; existing funded trades retain their ABI/IDL and exit metadata.
A signed off-chain pause/deprecation may hide new-funding buttons and warn users but cannot lock deployed exits or force a migration.
Emergency UI releases default to recovery/watch-only for the affected new-entry feature; existing compatible release/refund commands remain accessible after fresh chain/wallet checks.
Production release policy requires two distinct reviewed attestations: implementation/change owner and security/release reviewer.
A sole developer may produce local/testnet builds with one signature but cannot label that independent review.
If no independent reviewer is available, record the gate pending rather than invent an identity.
Key revocation is published through the prior trusted release-key policy; replacing a public key downloaded from the same compromised site is not independent recovery.
Decisions are public sanitized repo artifacts, never private trade logs.
Schema rejects unknown fields, duplicate reviewer identities and nonexistent evidence paths.
Hashes are exact lowercase SHA-256 artifact digests; chain runtime hashes remain G11 family-specific.
Missing accepted decisions block release-enabled configuration changes; they do not delete existing recovery data.
A maintainer/release key compromise can deliver malicious client code even with immutable escrow, so immutability alone does not protect signing requests.
Separate software provenance from contract authority, retain old artifact/recovery instructions and expose all enabled privilege surfaces.
A malicious relay can censor coordination; it cannot acquire a settlement role.
Multiple names controlled by one person are not independent review.
Optional upgrade/admin mechanisms stay outside core and need separate explicit terms before funds are committed.
Contract tests and ABI/IDL inspection assert absence of admin sweep/upgrade/pause-exit paths.
Test signed deprecation prevents new default funding without disabling compatible old release/refund recovery.
Simulate compromised release-key notice, missing reviewer and false duplicate identities.
Validate decision records and exact artifact linkage.

Sources: [system context](../../feature_0.4_architecture_planning/module_0.4.1_system_boundaries/spec-system-context-contract.md), [registry](../../../01_P2P_SHIELDED_OFFRAMP_ENGINE/feature_1.6_wallet_connectivity/module_1.6.2_rpc_registry/spec-chain-network-registry.md), [release policy](../../feature_0.3_system_integration/module_0.3.3_release_distribution/spec-ipfs-origin-and-update-policy.md).
Turn protocol changes into explicit versioned decisions and compatibility evidence.
No software update silently changes a signed trade's settlement semantics or upgrades already funded escrow.
One proposal addresses one observable protocol change.
Versioned wire/storage/contract schemas are independent of the frontend package version.
Evidence paths and exact selected dependency/deployment revisions are part of the decision.
UI wording changes that alter privacy or economic claims are security-impacting even if no ABI changes.
Draft includes before/after examples, affected authorities, alternative designs, privacy impact and rollback/recovery plan.
Review checks schema compatibility, old exits, mixed-client negotiation, reorg/restart behavior and required evidence.
Accepted means design approved; implemented requires actual committed code/tests; neither means independently audited.
Breaking wire changes use a new supported protocol version and explicit negotiation.
Unknown required versions refuse before signing/funding.
Storage changes follow G09, preserving source profiles and downgrade export.
Escrow changes deploy a new immutable version and do not migrate funded positions through frontend assumptions.
Crypto changes update G06 profile/version and independent vectors, with no silent primitive/KDF downgrade.
Roll out to local fixtures, testnet/browser matrix, then separately reviewed release.
Removing support requires published recovery artifacts for funded positions, not a package deletion that strands them.
An emergency rollback selects a prior complete artifact/configuration set; it never writes a newer vault using an old schema or relabels chain state.
`validateProposal(input): CoreResult<ProtocolProposalV1>` enforces IDs <=64 ASCII bytes, at most 128 affected specs/evidence entries, valid repo-relative paths and known kind/status.
`evaluateCompatibility(readerVersion, writerVersion, proposal)` returns compatible/read-only/unsupported with fixed rationale code.
Implementation CI verifies exact spec paths and evidence files exist and that enabled profiles match release manifests.
Missing evidence holds status at review; a failed upgrade leaves old authenticated data intact.
Stakeholder comments are inputs, not votes that can seize funds or override contract authority.
Semantic version labels can hide authority changes, mixed-version peers may negotiate down protection, and discarded recovery assets can lock users out.
Bind exact capabilities and versions into terms; reject unknown required features.
Reviewed proposal records reduce ambiguity but do not validate implementation correctness.
Hostile proposals may contain links/code; review in inert text and never execute imported artifacts merely to inspect them.
Use a version compatibility table with old/new readers and writers.
Test unknown required wire version, newer-record downgrade write refusal, old funded escrow recovery after UI upgrade, missing/dead recovery artifacts and altered crypto fixture hashes.
Rejected/withdrawn proposals must not enable capabilities.

Sources: [roadmap](../../../DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md), [G09 migrations](../../feature_0.4_architecture_planning/module_0.4.4_state_management/spec-storage-schema-migrations.md), [G14 extensions](../../feature_0.4_architecture_planning/module_0.4.6_extension_contract/spec-optional-module-interface.md).
Provide a versioned source-backed review workflow for supported operations without inventing a legal classification from the words noncustodial, anonymous or decentralized.
This specification defines an evidence interface; it does not conclude that any commercial operation is approved in any jurisdiction.
Default production matrix has no approved commercial profiles.
Local/simulated/testnet engineering remains clearly labeled and cannot be represented as commercial approval.
Sources identify actual official guidance/legislation and effective dates; digest records captured evidence, not a legal opinion.

Collect LEGAL02 operational facts before classifying an activity: who controls keys/assets, routes fiat, matches counterparties, receives fees, operates relays, adjudicates or physically carries cash.
Map each actual role/activity/jurisdiction to source-backed requirements and record a qualified reviewer decision.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Funded: fundNative / fundToken (msg.sender == terms.seller, now < acceptBefore, 1800 ≤ expiry−now ≤ 604800)
    Funded --> Released: release (seller, now < deadline)
    Funded --> Refunded: refund (anyone, now ≥ deadline, pays seller)
    Released --> [*]
    Refunded --> [*]
    note right of Released: payout pushed, or credited to pendingWithdrawals[buyer][asset]
    note right of Refunded: payout pushed, or credited to pendingWithdrawals[seller][asset]
```

`tradeId` is the G16 EVM `termsHash`: `keccak256(0x1901 ‖ domainSeparator ‖ hashStruct(TradeTerms))` with domain `EIP712Domain(name "P2POfframp", version "1", chainId = block.chainid, verifyingContract = escrow)`.
It is computed on-chain from the supplied terms; callers cannot choose an id.
Native asset uses `assetKind = 0` and the zero-address sentinel; never address guessing.
The field-by-field mapping is recorded in the contract README.
Types containing native ABI/IDL declarations describe that chain interface, not a shared executable TypeScript module.
Public strings/keys must use the selected chain/protocol canonical encoding; unknown fields and incompatible versions fail closed.

Funding MUST: require `terms.seller == msg.sender`; buyer nonzero, not the seller and not the escrow; `revision ≥ 1`; amount > 0; `block.timestamp < acceptBeforeSeconds`; `MIN_DURATION (1800) ≤ escrowExpirySeconds − block.timestamp ≤ MAX_DURATION (604800)`; compute `tradeId`; reject a used `tradeId` (forever, including after settlement) and a used `(seller, sellerNonce)`; store all terms and mark Funded before the asset transfer; for native require `msg.value == amount`; for ERC-20 require allowlisted asset, `SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom` and `balanceAfter − balanceBefore == amount` (fee-on-transfer reverts).
Any failure reverts all effects including nonce consumption.
Release MUST require Funded, caller == seller and `block.timestamp < deadline`.
Refund MUST require Funded and `block.timestamp ≥ deadline`, accept any caller and pay only the stored seller.
Both set the terminal state and emit their event before any external call, under `ReentrancyGuard`.

Payout (normative change from v1.0 "revert restores FUNDED"): require `gasleft() ≥ MIN_PAYOUT_GAS (120000)`; native push uses `call` with a fixed `NATIVE_PUSH_GAS (50000)` stipend and copies no return data; ERC-20 push uses `trySafeTransfer`.
If the push fails, credit `pendingWithdrawals[recipient][asset] += amount` and emit `PayoutDeferred`.
`withdraw` zeroes the credit before transferring and reverts (restoring it) on failure.
Rationale: a rejecting/gas-burning/blacklisted recipient can neither block a seller's final decision nor trap principal, and no path redirects funds.

Invariants (tested): per asset, escrow balance == Σ Funded principal + Σ pending credits (forced ETH excepted, which is unowned surplus); each trade reaches at most one terminal state; principal out equals funded principal exactly (zero protocol fee); no admin or sweep path exists.

Decimal money is never a JavaScript float; strings are parsed to bounded integers and overflow is rejected.

Clients map them to fixed G13 codes; repeated settlement reverts `InvalidState` and the UI rereads terminal state.
Recovery: expiry creates refund eligibility, not automatic execution; any account can submit `refund` directly against the ABI if the frontend disappears.
A deferred payout is recovered with `withdraw(recipient, asset)` by any account once the recipient can accept; clients MUST surface `PayoutDeferred` and pending balances.

Cancellation stops owned work and rejects late generation outputs, but cannot retract already transmitted data or transactions.

| Attack | Mitigation | Evidence |
| Re-entrancy via receiver or token hook | CEI + `nonReentrant` on all mutators | attacker tests (push, withdraw, callback during fund and payout) |
| Reverting / gas-burning recipient blocks settlement | Bounded push + deferred credit | reverting buyer/seller, gas burner tests |
| Griefer under-supplies gas to force deferral | `MIN_PAYOUT_GAS` check | `test_insufficientGas_cannotForceDeferral` |
| Fee-on-transfer / short deposit | Exact balance delta | unit + fuzz |
| Rebasing / callback / upgradeable token | Allowlist policy (immutable) | policy, not code; per-token review required |
| Cross-chain / cross-deployment replay | EIP-712 domain binds chainId + escrow | `test_tradeId_isDeploymentAndChainBound` |
| Seller nonce reuse across orders | `sellerNonceUsed` | unit |
| Release vs refund race at deadline | Disjoint guards; inclusion order decides | both orders tested |
| Forced ETH | No liability created; no sweep | unit + invariant |
Seller can withhold after fiat arrives; explicit G17 acknowledgement is required.
A malicious token or callback cannot access another trade or settle twice.

Separate public minimal advertisements from confidential peer terms using standard Nostr message layers, and let a buyer and seller agree the exact G16 terms bytes privately before any wallet signature or funding.
This contract uses CTX01 `TradeBinding`, CTX02 observations, G08 authority, G10 wallet sessions, G11 approved registry and G12 transaction intents.
`CoreResult`/error codes follow G13.
Native transactions/signatures retain their chain formats; local or relay observations never establish custody or fiat receipt.
A session that reaches `accepted` is a negotiation record only: it is not funding, not a wallet signature and not escrow state.
Chain observation (`packages/domain/src/authority.ts`) remains the sole source of funding and settlement.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Buyer (messaging key)
  participant R as Relays (kind 1059, discovery only)
  participant S as Seller (ad maker key)
  S->>R: kind 30078 ad (public, G19)
  B->>R: gift wrap: take-request (ad address, buyer EVM address)
  R->>S: wrap -> unwrap -> session "taken"
  S->>S: local review of terms bytes (G16 + G11), compute termsHash
  S->>R: gift wrap: terms-offer (exact review-document bytes, termsHash)
  R->>B: wrap -> unwrap -> LOCAL REVIEW -> recompute termsHash
  B->>R: gift wrap: terms-accept (termsHash, revision) or terms-reject
  R->>S: session "accepted" (no funding implied)
  Note over B,S: Wallet acceptance signatures (G16) and funding are separate, chain-observed steps.
```
Every message is the content of a NIP-17 kind-14 rumor, sealed (kind 13, NIP-44 v2 to the recipient) and gift-wrapped (kind 1059, one-time key, single `p` tag).
Each send produces a recipient wrap and a self-copy wrap.
Rumor tags are exactly `["p",recipient]`, `["a","30078:<sellerPubkey>:p2p-offramp:v1:<orderId>"]`, `["t","p2p-offramp-terms-v1"]` and, once terms exist, `["trade","<termsHash>"]`.

```typescript
interface ExchangeEnvelopeV1 {            // exact keys; UTF-8 JSON; <= 24576 bytes; rumor JSON <= 40960 bytes
  v: 1;
  type: "take-request" | "terms-offer" | "terms-accept" | "terms-reject" | "cancel";
  ad: string;                              // kind-30078 address of the advert
  orderId: string;                         // 64 hex, equals the address orderId
  sender: string; recipient: string;       // x-only Nostr keys, 64 lowercase hex, distinct; sender == authenticated seal author
  nonce: string;                           // 32 random bytes, hex
  expiresAtSeconds: string;                // <= receipt time + 3600 and > receipt time
  termsHash: string | null;                // G16 evmTermsHash (hex); null for take-request, optional for cancel, required otherwise
  body:
    | { buyerAddress: string; buyerMessagingKey: string }   // take-request: lowercase non-zero 0x EVM address; key == sender
    | { terms: string }                                     // terms-offer: the exact G16 review-document bytes as UTF-8, <= 16384 bytes
    | { revision: string }                                  // terms-accept: canonical u64 revision, must equal the reviewed revision
    | { reason: "declined" | "review-failed" | "expired" }  // terms-reject
    | { reason: "withdrawn" | "declined" | "expired" };     // cancel
}
type SessionState = "taken" | "offered" | "accepted" | "rejected" | "cancelled";   // per (ad address, buyer key)
```

State machine (sender role is derived from the ad, never from the message): `none -take-request(buyer)-> taken -terms-offer(seller)-> offered -terms-accept(buyer)-> accepted`; `offered -terms-reject(buyer)-> rejected`; `taken|offered -cancel(either)-> cancelled`.
Every other combination is `OUT_OF_ORDER`.
`accepted`, `rejected` and `cancelled` are terminal; a cancelled or rejected pair may start a fresh `take-request`.

Limits: 64 live sessions (new sessions are refused, nothing is evicted while live), 1024 remembered rumor ids (only expired ids are pruned, so a live replay is always recognised), message ttl 900 s by default and never beyond the ad expiry, 120 s future skew for the sender-claimed rumor time.
Types containing native ABI/IDL declarations describe that chain interface, not a shared executable TypeScript module.
Public strings/keys use the selected canonical encoding; unknown fields and incompatible versions fail closed.

**Send.** Validate the session and role, run local review where terms are involved, build the envelope, create the rumor with `createUnsignedEvent`, then seal and wrap it twice (recipient, self) with fresh one-time keys.
The local state advances only after wrapping succeeds.

**Receive, cheapest check first.** (1) Unwrap and verify all three layers (`unwrapGiftWrap`: wrap and seal signatures and ids, `seal.pubkey == rumor.pubkey`, NIP-44 MACs); failures are `WRAP_INVALID`. (2) A rumor authored by ourselves is a self-copy and changes nothing. (3) Strict envelope parse (`MALFORMED`), `sender == rumor.pubkey`, `recipient == self` (`NOT_ADDRESSED`), tags exactly as derived from the envelope, lifetime bounds (`EXPIRED`, `MALFORMED`). (4) Dedupe by rumor id (`DUPLICATE`), before any state work; an id is recorded only when the message is applied, so a legitimately early message is not lost. (5) Authority: only the ad's seller key may send `terms-offer` and, towards a buyer, anything at all (`NOT_SELLER`); only the key that sent the `take-request` may accept or reject (`NOT_COUNTERPARTY`); a key with no session cannot do anything but take (`UNKNOWN_SESSION`). (6) The state machine (`OUT_OF_ORDER`). (7) Type-specific bindings below.

**Bindings.** `take-request` requires a live advert from `OrderBook.revalidate` whose author and `maker` are this key (`AD_UNAVAILABLE`, `AD_EXPIRED`); sessions carry the ad's expiry and refuse every step at or after it.

`terms-offer` runs `reviewTermsBytes` against the injected G11 registry (`REVIEW_FAILED` with the domain rejection code), then requires: `orderId` equals the ad, `buyer` equals the take-request's address (`TERMS_MISMATCH`), the amount lies inside the ad range (`AD_MISMATCH`), `acceptBefore` is in the future (`EXPIRED`), and the injected `hashTerms` result (for EVM, `packages/wallet` `evmTermsHash`, the exact digest the escrow computes) equals the envelope `termsHash` (`HASH_MISMATCH`).
`terms-accept` requires `termsHash` equal to the reviewed hash and `revision` equal to the reviewed revision (`HASH_MISMATCH`, `REVISION_MISMATCH`).
The buyer's `accept()` takes the bytes the user was shown and refuses unless they equal, byte for byte, the bytes local review approved (`TERMS_MISMATCH`), before anything is signed or sent.

NIP-44 does not expose arbitrary AAD: trade, ad, order, revision, sender and recipient are bound inside the authenticated encrypted plaintext and verified after decrypt, not through an invented AAD parameter.
The advertisement carries no decryption key.
No custom cipher and no NIP-04 fallback exist (kind 4 is rejected by nostr-crypto).
All externally supplied records require exact schema/version validation and byte/count caps before cryptographic work.
Decimal money is never a JavaScript float; strings are parsed to bounded integers and overflow is rejected.
G13 read retries are bounded; economic commands have zero automatic resubmission.

```typescript
createTermsExchange({ provider, selfPublicKey, ads: Pick<OrderBook,"revalidate">, registry: RegistryLookup,
                      hashTerms: (ReviewedEvmTerms) => string, now: () => number, maxSessions?, maxSeenMessages?, messageTtlSeconds? }): TermsExchange
take(adKey, buyerAddress, secret) / offer(sessionId, termsBytes, secret) / accept(sessionId, termsBytes, secret) /
reject(sessionId, reason, secret) / cancel(sessionId, reason, secret)  // -> { recipientWrap, selfWrap, state, rumorId } to publish via the relay pool
receive(giftWrap, secret) -> ReceivedMessage | { own: true }
session(id) -> SessionView | null;  close()
createRelayEventCrypto({ provider, secretKey }) -> relay EventCrypto (synchronous verify, provider-signed events, dispose())
```

| Attack | Mitigation |
| Impostor offers terms to a buyer | Only the ad's seller key (the seal author, authenticated) may offer; an envelope `sender` that differs from the seal author is `MALFORMED`. |
| Replay or re-wrap of an old message | Dedupe by rumor id (a re-wrap under a new one-time key is the same rumor); messages expire within 3600 s and are refused after; live ids are never evicted. |
| Tampered terms | The buyer recomputes the G16 digest from locally reviewed bytes and compares it with the envelope hash; accept covers exactly the reviewed bytes. |
| Accept a different revision or different terms | Hash and revision are checked on the seller side; a different G16 trade has a different digest. |
| Third party injects a message | No session for that key (`UNKNOWN_SESSION`), or not the seller (`NOT_SELLER`); a take from a new key creates only a bounded, separate session. |
| Expired or stale ad | Sessions carry the ad expiry; every send and receive re-checks it. |
| Session or memory exhaustion | 64 sessions, 1024 ids, 16 KiB terms, 24 KiB envelope; refusal, not eviction. |
| Fake wallet identity | A messaging key proves control of an ad, not of the seller's wallet; the wallet binding exists only through the G16 acceptance signatures verified separately. |

Time comes from an injected trusted clock in unix seconds; if it is absent, non-integer or throws, freshness is **unknown** and the book accepts nothing, lists nothing and refuses revalidation (`clock-unknown`).
**Revision ordering.** The author's signed `revision` is the only ordering authority for one `(pubkey, d)` key; relay-reported order and `created_at` are not.
A higher revision replaces the current ad even if its `created_at` is older.
A lower revision is `stale-revision` (so a relay replaying an old signed revision cannot win).
The same revision with the same event id is `duplicate`.
The same revision with a different event id is a `conflict`: the entry becomes non-actionable (`revalidate` returns `conflict`, `list` omits it) until a strictly higher revision arrives.
Nothing silently picks a winner.
**Expiry.** Expired entries are dropped on every ingest, list and revalidate.
A signed already-expired offer is `expired` and never stored.
A local clock ahead of the signed time expires an ad early; a lagging clock does not extend the signed expiry because `revalidate` compares against the signed `expiresAtSeconds` only.
**Revalidation before use.** `revalidate(key)` MUST be called immediately before any negotiation step that consumes an ad.
It re-checks clock, deletion tombstone, expiry and conflict and returns the current verified ad or a reason.
A listed ad that was valid a minute ago is not valid now.
Funding is out of scope of this module and separately revalidates the on-chain deadline and original G16 terms.
**Deletion.** On cancellation the maker publishes a NIP-09 request and lets the NIP-40 expiration lapse.
This is best effort and **does not guarantee removal**: a relay may ignore kind 5, serve the old ad indefinitely, or have it archived.

**G05 gate.** Every socket, read or publish, starts with `broker.authorize({channel:"relay", endpointId, method})` and `capture`; a string refusal means no socket exists.

`POLICY_BLOCKED` and `INVALID_ENDPOINT` (strict mode without verified-private coverage, unknown coverage, an endpoint the registry does not know, the production-default empty registry) put the relay into `blocked` with no timer and no retry until an explicit `retry`.
The pool has no direct-connection path and no fallback relay list; candidates come only from the configuration given at construction, never from event content.

The connect handshake runs inside the single-shot `scope.run` (its operation never rejects, because a rejected operation makes the broker block the whole adapter); afterwards the scope is checked on every inbound frame and its abort closes the socket, so mode changes, revocation and expiry sever live connections (`revoked`) and the next attempt is re-authorized.

**Inbound order, cheapest first:** scope current; text frame (binary is penalized); frame length cap (before JSON.parse; oversized frames are dropped and penalized 10 = immediate ban); token bucket (excess frames are dropped before parsing); strict JSON/shape parse (NIP-01 `EVENT/EOSE/OK/NOTICE/CLOSED`; `AUTH`/`COUNT` ignored and never answered); the subscription id must be one this pool sent on this connection (else penalty 3); dedupe by id (before any signature work); the event must match one of the subscription's filters (else penalty 3); per-subscription event cap (on exceeding, `CLOSE` is sent and the subscription is ignored on that connection; not a ban); `verifyEvent` (failure: penalty 4, and the id is **not** remembered, so a forged copy cannot suppress the genuine event); only then the id is recorded and `onEvent` is called once per distinct id across all relays.
Relay text (`NOTICE`, `CLOSED` reasons, `OK` messages) is never surfaced or interpreted.
`CLOSED` ends that subscription on that relay; it is not resubscribed automatically.
**Penalties.** oversized 10, malformed 3, binary 3, invalid signature 4, wrong subscription 3, outside filter 3, unsolicited `OK` 2.
At 10 the relay is `banned` for the pool's lifetime (not cleared by `retry`) and the next candidate is promoted.
Three consecutive 10-second windows that each dropped at least one frame disconnect the relay (not a ban; reconnect backoff applies).
**Reconnect and failover.** Connections exist only while at least one subscription is active; closing the last subscription tears all sockets down and resets backoff.

On an unexpected close or error the relay waits `floor(random × ceiling[k−1])` ms (full jitter; ceilings 1/2/4/8/16/30 s), up to six reconnects; the seventh consecutive failure marks it `failed` (explicit `retry` needed, no background retry).
Failure counters reset only after 60 s of stable uptime.

When a relay becomes `blocked`, `failed` or `banned`, the next idle approved candidate is promoted so that up to four are active; subscriptions are replayed on every new connection and history replay is absorbed by dedupe.

**Publish.** One explicit operation sends the identical signed event at most once to each selected relay over its own `publish`-method permit and short-lived connection, waits for the matching `OK` or the timeout, and closes.
`accepted` means that relay accepted it, nothing more.
Events that fail local shape or `verifyEvent` checks are refused before any connection.

requirements.text: Implementation-specific residual risks: (a) the unknown-hash `confirmed` label is evidence that the nonce was consumed and the escrow shows the effect, not proof that this exact transaction caused it (another app may have funded the same terms); the outcome is still the observed escrow state. (b) `dropped` is a single-node view (pool and nonce); the same-nonce successor rule, not the label, is what prevents a double inclusion. (c) EIP-1193 4001 is trusted as "nothing submitted"; a dishonest wallet can lie about anything, so chain invariants (`TradeIdUsed`, seller-only release) remain the backstop. (d) Lifecycle reservation trusts `finalized`/`failed` records in the authenticated vault; restored backups are not yet distinguished from locally written records. (e) The wallet may override the requested nonce; reconciliation then observes the real body and reports `INTEGRITY_FAILURE` or `replaced` rather than latching.

Keep spending authority in external wallets and isolate storage, messaging, and recovery lifecycles.
Prevent reuse of wallet signatures, storage passphrases, or identity keys as interchangeable secrets.
This contract creates no custom signature scheme and does not promise forensic memory erasure.
| Material | Owner | Persistence | Authority |
| Wallet spending key | External wallet | Never in app vault, logs, QR, or backups | Chain transactions only |
| Random vault DEK | G02 storage service | Wrapped by passphrase-derived KEK | Authenticated local snapshot |
| KEK | G02 unlock operation | No persistence | Unwrap DEK only |
| Messaging identity key | Reviewed Nostr signer adapter | Encrypted G02 identity record only if app-managed; otherwise signer-held | Message signing/decryption only |
| Per-message ephemeral key | Messaging adapter | In memory for its specified operation | Protocol-defined message role |
| Session token | Vault service | Memory only | Local vault handle, no external identity |
The app MUST NOT derive messaging keys from DEKs, passphrases, EVM signatures, Solana signatures, or wallet seed material.
G02 generates a random DEK; this spec does not replace it with a deterministic hierarchy.
App-managed messaging identity backup is opt-in private recovery material, not a spending-wallet backup.
Identity state is `absent -> locked -> unlocked -> locked`, with `retired` available only after explicit rotation.
Generate a messaging identity through the selected reviewed protocol library using Web Crypto randomness; reject invalid scalars according to that library.
No handwritten secp256k1 or scalar-reduction implementation is allowed.
The specific library/version and vector fixture hashes must enter G06 before messaging is enabled.
Each unlock creates a fresh 32-random-byte opaque session token and a nonnegative generation.
Lock marks the session invalid synchronously, increments generation, drops key/plaintext references, and invalidates all pending outputs.
Async crypto may finish but MUST not publish results under an invalid generation.
G02 lock and in-flight-commit outcome rules remain authoritative.
Page hide locks all sessions; five minutes without trusted pointer/keyboard input locks idle sessions.
Untrusted synthetic events, read polling, timers, and background RPC do not refresh idle activity.
Reopening requires unlock, not automatic decryption using a cached passphrase.
Wallet account/network changes also cancel identity-bound preparations; they do not silently rotate the messaging identity.
Rotation generates an independent identity and records retirement locally.
Old messages remain recoverable only if the old identity is retained in encrypted backup.
Do not promise that rotation erases historical public associations.
No circuit or on-chain contract applies.
The caller first unlocks G02 using its VaultService; these identity methods require that live authenticated VaultSession, never an implicit profile or cached passphrase.
The service verifies the session/profile binding on every call and keeps it in each internal handle.
Two concurrently unlocked profiles cannot share an identity handle.
The identityRecordId is a G02 record ID in that exact profile.
These methods wrap G02 and a protocol signer; no API returns raw keys to UI components.
`create` requires an unlocked vault and atomically persists its encrypted identity before reporting success.
Errors are fixed `LOCKED`, `CANCELLED`, `UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER`, `INVALID_IDENTITY`, `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONFLICT`, or `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
Cancellation after durable creation returns a discoverable identity reference, not a false claim that no key was stored.
Private signing/decryption operations belong to the messaging adapter and require a valid purpose-bound handle.
At most one active identity is selected per profile; imported retired keys remain read-only unless explicitly reselected.
A signature-request phishing attack must not gain a general signer API from the UI; approved protocol operations validate the complete message schema and recipient.
Memory compromise/XSS can read app-managed unlocked keys; nonextractable key handles do not protect against arbitrary same-origin code using them.
Buffers may be overwritten best effort, but JS strings, browser heaps, swap, crash dumps, and copied buffers cannot be reliably erased.
Never persist passphrases in localStorage, IndexedDB, service worker caches, analytics, error reports, or form autofill controlled by app code.
Lost unbacked-up messaging keys mean lost local decryptability; external-wallet recovery is independent.

Prevent untrusted order/chat/QR/receipt data from becoming active content and restrict outbound resources in the static client.
CSP is defense in depth and does not establish private transport, wallet correctness, or protection against a compromised build.
All imported content passes bounded schema validation before state reducers and text rendering.
React components render strings as text; HTML/Markdown rendering, SVG imports, embedded remote images, user CSS, scripts, and arbitrary link previews are disabled in the core client.
Public order text is capped at 4096 UTF-8 bytes; private chat at 16384 bytes before encryption; these do not override smaller protocol limits.

Tests may include malicious strings as inert fixtures.
The deployment pipeline emits a per-release CSP from the validated endpoint registry.
Minimum directives:
`<explicit ...>` is generated deployment data, never shipped literally.
No wildcard host, `data:` script, `blob:` script/worker, `unsafe-inline`, or `unsafe-eval` is permitted.
External wallets requiring frames or additional connections need a reviewed capability-specific policy and tests before enablement; core has no embedded wallet frame.
WASM proof providers remain disabled in core; do not loosen all script execution to enable a future provider.
Prefer HTTP CSP headers with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
Static hosts that cannot set headers use a CSP meta tag before all resource tags and `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">`.
`frame-ancestors` cannot be enforced by CSP meta, so such deployment MUST display that clickjacking protection is unverified, not claim equivalent header protection.
Link navigation always uses an explicit UI action, exact validated HTTPS URL, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and no private query data.
Host CSP limitations remain a release-profile capability.
Custom endpoint changes outside the build allowlist require a rebuilt policy; never silently broaden `connect-src` at runtime.
CSP does not prevent every same-origin exfiltration mechanism.
A build validator accepts only registry-owned origin entries, rejects credentials/path/query/fragment/wildcards, and emits deterministic sorted directives.
`framingProtected` is true only when deployed header behavior is verified.
Runtime content validators reject invalid UTF-8, disallowed controls, and oversized input before rendering.
Dangerous URIs (`javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`, `intent:` and malformed URLs) produce `INVALID_INPUT` without rendering clickable links.
CSP violations become fixed local diagnostic counters; do not upload original blocked URI or document URL.
Build validation failure blocks release output.
HTML/script injection through chats or QR codes stays text.
Homoglyph and bidirectional address confusion requires full canonical address display and chain-specific confirmation; CSP cannot solve it.
Remote image tracking is blocked by disallowing user images and external image origins.
Malicious dependencies and same-origin scripts still have app privileges: G06 provenance and static build review remain necessary.
Meta-only hosting cannot promise anti-framing.
Browser extensions, wallet UI, OS/browser bugs, and compromised DNS/TLS or host build delivery remain outside CSP's guarantee.

Test HTML, SVG, event attributes, script tags, bidi address samples, Markdown image links, embedded nulls, malformed Unicode, oversized bytes, and all dangerous URI schemes in every user-controlled field.

Browser integration MUST attempt external script/font/image/iframe, inline script/event/style, eval, form submit, worker and WebSocket connections; assert the applicable policy blocks each and required local resources still load.
Test header and meta deployment profiles separately.
Test actual deployed responses, not configuration files alone.
Audit production bundles for banned sinks and unapproved external origins; no source-only grep may be called complete XSS testing.

The system authority contract governs this module: external wallets authorize spending; deployed escrow and reconciled chain observations establish custody state; relay and local data are untrusted claims.
This specification creates no operator release path, automatic bank payment or authority over an already funded trade.
Missing optional infrastructure MUST preserve basic release/refund and encrypted recovery paths.

Private application payload v1 has format p2p-offramp-message, version 1, trade binding, termsHash (64 lowercase hex), messageId (16 random bytes lowercase hex), sender identity, recipient identity, kind (text/terms/receipt-status), createdAt (safe integer milliseconds) and body.
Text is at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes, whole payload at most 24576 bytes; protocol limits may be smaller.
Runtime validation MUST reject unknown versions/properties, unsafe integers, duplicate identities and oversized inputs before expensive work.
Network, deployment, trade and account generation are explicit bindings where economic state is involved.
Amounts are unsigned decimal base-unit strings, never floating point.
Immutable results and defensive copies prevent consumers mutating validated state.
Protocol-specific limits override broader application limits.
Validate exact keys/types and recipient/trade/terms binding after authenticated protocol decryption.
Route only supported kinds to their validator; unknown kinds are rejected, not rendered as HTML.
Deduplicate on authenticated sender plus messageId within the encrypted history.
A sender timestamp is untrusted ordering information; keep receipt order separately.
Delivery acknowledgement is not fiat proof.
Asynchronous jobs carry a generation and AbortSignal.
Revoked generations MUST NOT publish late plaintext, restore stale coverage or initiate new economic work.
Dispose removes subscriptions and closes owned resources.
Cancellation after broadcast is an uncertain transaction outcome requiring journal reconciliation, not proof of rollback.
Existing signed/funded terms cannot be renegotiated by changing a local preference.
encodeMessage(validatedPayload) produces deterministic UTF-8 JSON with documented schema field order; decodeMessage(bytes, expectedBinding) returns validated payload or fixed error.
Persist only authenticated payload in G02 chat records.
Transport envelopes remain protocol-specific.
All interfaces return the shared core result/error contract.

Distinguish INVALID_INPUT, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER, UNAUTHORIZED, LOCKED, CANCELLED and unavailable external service; map concrete errors to registered G13 codes without exposing private content.
No unbounded retry, secret-bearing diagnostics, destructive reset or silent downgrade is permitted.
Operations that propose economic effects pass core preflight, durable G12 reservation and fresh external-wallet consent; this module cannot bypass them.
Encryption does not authorize sender claims, escrow transitions or external links.
Limit parser size before decode; render text inertly through G04.
Message IDs prevent duplicate UI effects, not global replay across unbound contexts.
Active origin compromise, malicious extensions and a compromised OS can read unlocked state; capability wrappers are not a same-origin JavaScript sandbox.
Transport encryption, payload encryption and chain privacy are independent properties.
G02 remains the exact v1 storage authority: no alternative KDF, AAD, record kind or session token is introduced here.
G03 alone governs authenticated fresh-key restore.
No physical erasure, global anonymity or provider availability guarantee is made.
Test wrong recipient/trade/hash, duplicate IDs with changed content, invalid UTF-8, unknown fields/kinds, overlong text, markup and out-of-order delivery.
No message may trigger a wallet operation.
For each supported profile record source/dependency commit, integrity digest, protocol revision, deployment/network IDs, fixture provenance, browser/provider matrix and named review.
Mutable documentation links below identify primary protocols; they are not an evaluated implementation pin.
Where no concrete profile is approved the implementation MUST return unsupported, not emulate success.
Unit fixtures alone do not establish browser routing, wallet support or custody safety.

- **In scope:** NIP-01 event serialization, id hashing, BIP340 signing and verification, and strict parsing of untrusted events.
NIP-44 version 2 payloads with plaintexts of 1..65535 bytes.
- **Not implemented:** NIP-04 (no code path; kind 4 is rejected everywhere).

Relay I/O.

Persistence.

- Errors are a fixed `NostrCryptoError` code set, a subset of the G13 codes ([G13](../../../00_PLANNING_AND_THREAT_MODELING/feature_0.4_architecture_planning/module_0.4.5_failure_contract/spec-typed-errors-and-retries.md)).

generate, publicKey] --> P[NostrMessagingProvider
+ signSchnorr, verifySchnorr, conversationKey] P -->|BIP340| E[event.ts
NIP-01 id, sign, verifyEvent] P -->|ECDH x, HKDF-extract| CK[conversation key 32 B] CK --> N[nip44.ts

Keys: the secret key is the G01 messaging identity (or a one-time gift-wrap key).
It is never the G02 DEK or an external spending key.
Public keys are BIP340 x-only, 64 lowercase hex.
A key is accepted only if `x < p` and `x` lifts to a curve point (even y).
Secret keys must be scalars in `[1, n−1]`.
The pinned dependencies are `@noble/curves` 2.4.0 (BIP340, ECDH), `@noble/hashes` 2.4.0 (SHA-256, HKDF, HMAC) and `@noble/ciphers` 2.4.0 (ChaCha20).

**NIP-01.** `id = sha256(utf8(JSON.stringify([0, pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content])))`.
JSON.stringify output equals the NIP-01 escaping rules only when no string contains a control character other than `\b \t \n \f \r`, and no lone surrogate.
Strings containing either are rejected, so for every accepted event the serialization is exactly the NIP-01 one.
`signEvent` derives the author key from the secret, hashes, signs, and verifies its own signature before returning.
`verifyEvent(untrusted)` runs these steps in order:
Require a plain object with exactly the 7 keys.
Accessors, prototypes and extra or missing keys are rejected.
Check lowercase hex lengths, a safe integer `created_at`, and a `kind` in 0..65535.
Kind 4 fails with `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`, and `allowedKinds` is enforced.
Check bounds: tag count, items per tag, item bytes, and content bytes.
Each tag must be a non-empty array of strings.
Recompute the id, which must equal the claimed id.
Verify the BIP340 signature.
Signature work happens only after every bound check passes.
`parseUnsignedEvent` applies the same rules to a 6-key rumor; a `sig` key is rejected.
`parseEventJson` is a bounded RFC 8259 parser.
It rejects duplicate keys (including escaped duplicates), `__proto__`, nesting deeper than 4, more than 4096 nodes, trailing data, and input over `maxJsonBytes`.
**NIP-44 v2**, implemented as the normative construction:
`conversation_key = HKDF-extract(SHA-256, IKM = x(a·B), salt = "nip44-v2")`.
The x coordinate is unhashed and 32 bytes.
Generate a 32-byte CSPRNG nonce.
The `nonce` argument of `encrypt` exists only to replay vectors.
`HKDF-expand(conversation_key, info = nonce, L = 76)` gives `chacha_key[0:32]`, `chacha_nonce[32:44]` and `hmac_key[44:76]`.
Pad as `u16be(len) ‖ plaintext ‖ zeros` to `calc_padded_len(len)`: 32 bytes minimum, then powers of two, then chunks of `next_power/8`.
`len` must be in 1..65535, otherwise `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
Lone surrogates are rejected rather than replaced.
Encrypt with ChaCha20 (RFC 8439) from block counter 0.
`mac = HMAC-SHA256(hmac_key, nonce ‖ ciphertext)`.
Output canonical base64 with padding of `0x02 ‖ nonce ‖ ciphertext ‖ mac`.
**Decryption** returns plaintext only after every check passes:
An empty payload or a leading `#` is `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`.
A payload outside 132..87472 characters (or a lower caller cap) is `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`.
This check runs before base64 decoding.
Base64 decoding is strict: no whitespace, no URL alphabet, and no non-canonical trailing bits.
A decoded length outside 99..65603 bytes is rejected.
A version byte other than 2 is `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`.
The MAC is compared over all 32 bytes in constant time, before any decryption.
The ciphertext is decrypted.
Unpadding requires a non-zero u16 length (zero is the unsupported extended-prefix marker), `len(padded) = 2 + calc_padded_len(len)`, all-zero padding, and fatal UTF-8 decoding.
Every failure after the version check is one class, `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`: size, base64, MAC, padding and UTF-8 errors are indistinguishable to the caller.
Message keys, the shared point, padded buffers and MAC buffers are zeroed in `finally` blocks.
Asynchronous jobs carry a generation and AbortSignal at the NIP-17 layer.
Revoked generations MUST NOT publish late plaintext.
Existing signed/funded terms cannot be renegotiated by changing a local preference.
The spec's earlier `encryptV2(recipientKey, plaintext, signerHandle)` form became a provider-plus-conversation-key form: the caller asks the provider for `conversationKey`, uses it, and wipes it.
A provider without `conversationKey` is `UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER` at the NIP-17 layer.
Nothing ever requests a wallet transaction signature as a substitute.
Error mapping: a malformed key, event or argument is `INVALID_INPUT`.
A size or count over a bound is `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
Kind 4, a leading `#`, or a version byte other than 2 is `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`.
A bad id, signature, MAC, padding, base64 or UTF-8 value is `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`.
A CSPRNG that is unavailable is `UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER`.
Every error has the fixed message `Nostr cryptographic operation failed.` and carries no input, key or plaintext.
No unbounded retry, secret-bearing diagnostics, destructive reset or silent downgrade is permitted.
NIP-44 protects content under its assumptions, not relay IP/timing or sender authenticity alone.
Reused entropy, unauthenticated outer events and active origin compromise defeat expectations.
| Attack | Mitigation in this implementation |
| MAC forgery or timing oracle | HMAC-SHA256 over nonce ‖ ciphertext. The compare runs the full 32 bytes in constant time, before decryption. A single error class follows the version check. |
| Malleable or alternative encodings | Strict canonical base64. Exact padding-length and zero-padding checks. Fatal UTF-8 decoding, including surrogate encodings. |
| Invalid-curve or twist points | Lift with `x < p` and an on-curve check. The official twist-order vectors (orders 3, 13, 3319) and all-ff key are rejected. |
| Out-of-range secret keys | Scalars must be in `[1, n−1]` (vectors `0`, `n`, `> n`). |
| Event id ambiguity | Rejected characters force serialization identical to NIP-01. The id is recomputed, never trusted. |
| JSON smuggling | Duplicate keys, `__proto__`, accessors, sparse arrays and extra keys are rejected. |
| Resource exhaustion | Size and count bounds run before base64 decoding, hashing or signature work. |
| NIP-04 downgrade | Kind 4 is rejected by every parser and builder. No NIP-04 code exists. |
| Nonce reuse | CSPRNG nonce by default. The `nonce` parameter is documented as vectors-only. |

| Bug in the project-owned cipher | RFC 8439 vector, byte-for-byte agreement with OpenSSL ChaCha20 at block boundaries, and all official NIP-44 vectors. Source hash pinned in the inventory. Independent review still required. |
Residual limits: this design has no forward secrecy and no post-compromise security.
Zeroization is best effort: `@noble/curves` uses bigints internally, and JavaScript strings (plaintext, hex keys) cannot be wiped.
Constant-time behavior is not guaranteed by the JIT.
Signatures use noble's BIP340 implementation with fresh auxiliary randomness.
