Boundaries of this iteration:
- **In scope:** the cryptographic and validation core.
That covers building and opening rumor, seal and gift-wrap layers, binding them to a G16 trade, an authorization rule limited to the two counterparties, and per-session deduplication.
- **Separate implemented composition:** `packages/messaging` validates the text-only application envelope and stores native authenticated proofs in existing encrypted G02 `chat` records.
Every history read reauthenticates those proofs with the original messaging identity.
Authenticated sender/message-ID deduplication survives vault reopen and G03 fresh-key restore; receipt order and timestamps have no economic authority.
Existing canonical G21 relay publication/read is exercised by the local exchange/escrow harness, with no automatic publication or retry in the chat package.
- **Not implemented:**
- chat reconnect cursors, outbox and durable delivery states (G21);
- kind 10050 relay-list discovery;
- non-text application envelope profiles; the bare native core still treats rumor `content` as opaque text bounded by its limits;
- `subject`/`e` reply tags;
- groups with more than two members.

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Seller session participant R as Relays (untrusted) participant B as Buyer session S->>S: rumor kind 14 (unsigned)
tags p=buyer, trade=tradeId, conversation=cid S->>S: seal kind 13 = sign_S(NIP44(conv(S,B), rumor)), tags [] S->>S: wrap kind 1059 = sign_E1(NIP44(conv(E1,B), seal)), tags [p=buyer] S->>S: self copy: seal to S, wrap under E2 with p=seller S-->>R: recipientWrap, selfWrap (publishing is G21, not here) R-->>B: wrap (any order, duplicates, forgeries) B->>B: verify wrap → decrypt → verify seal → decrypt → parse rumor B->>B: seal.pubkey == rumor.pubkey ∈ {S,B}; exact tags; dedup rumor.id ```
| Layer | Kind | Signed by | Tags | Content | created_at |
| rumor | 14 | nobody (id only) | the three tags above | text, ≤ 24576 UTF-8 bytes; rumor JSON ≤ 40960 bytes | send time |
| seal | 13 | author's messaging key | none (MUST be empty) | NIP-44(conv(author, recipient), rumor JSON) | uniform in [now − 172800, now] |
| gift wrap | 1059 | fresh one-time key | exactly one `["p", recipient]` | NIP-44(conv(one-time, recipient), seal JSON) | uniform in [now − 172800, now] |
Why 40960 bytes: a rumor JSON of that size pads to 40962 bytes and encodes to 54704 base64 characters.
The seal JSON therefore stays under the 65535-byte NIP-44 plaintext limit of the wrap.
Unwrapping accepts wraps and seals up to 600 seconds in the future (`MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECONDS`).

**Send** (`send(content, senderSecret, signal)`):
Check that the session is open and the signal is not aborted.
`content` must be non-empty.
Check that `provider.publicKey(senderSecret)` equals `selfPublicKey`; otherwise `UNAUTHORIZED`.
Build the rumor with the three binding tags.
Enforce the content and rumor-JSON limits (`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`).
Build the recipient seal and wrap, then the self-copy seal and wrap.
Each wrap uses its own one-time key from `provider.generate()`, and the one-time secret is wiped in `finally`.
Each conversation key is wiped after its single use.
The rumor is never signed.
Re-check close and abort after every await.
A closed session returns `LOCKED`; an aborted signal returns `CANCELLED`.
Either way nothing is returned for publication.
Record the rumor id as seen, so the self copy later reads as a duplicate.
**Receive** (`receive(untrustedWrap, recipientSecret, signal)`).
Each layer is fully verified before the next is decrypted:
`recipientSecret` must belong to `selfPublicKey`.
Verify the outer event: kind 1059 only (kind 4 is `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`), bounded, id and signature valid.
It must have exactly one `p` tag, of length 2, naming self; otherwise `UNAUTHORIZED`.
Its timestamp must not exceed the skew allowance.
NIP-44 decrypt with `conv(self, wrap.pubkey)`.
Parse the seal JSON strictly (duplicate keys rejected), then verify it: kind 13, zero tags, valid signature, skew check.
NIP-44 decrypt with `conv(self, seal.pubkey)`.
Parse the rumor strictly: kind 14, unsigned (a `sig` key is rejected), id recomputed, at most 3 tags of 2 items each, content within limits.
5. **Authenticate:** `rumor.pubkey == seal.pubkey`, otherwise `UNAUTHORIZED`.
A key that does not belong to the author cannot sign that author's seal.
6. **Authorize:** `rumor.pubkey` must be one of the two participants.
The tags must equal the expected three exactly: the `p` tag names the other participant, `trade` equals the bound tradeId, and `conversation` equals the derived id.
Anything else is `UNAUTHORIZED`.
7. **Deduplicate** by rumor id.
The rumor id is a hash of author, time, tags and content, so the same message re-delivered through any number of wraps or seals is one message.
A message already seen returns `{ duplicate: true }` and is not treated as new.
Once the session's seen-set reaches its bound, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` is returned rather than evicting, because forgetting an id would let a relay replay it as new.
Wrapper and seal timestamps and ids never establish application chronology.
`claimedCreatedAt` is a sender claim; receipt order is the caller's.
`close()` makes every in-flight and later call return `LOCKED` and clears the seen-set.
Reconnect, overlapping subscriptions and acknowledgements belong to G21 and are not implemented here.
Existing signed/funded terms cannot be renegotiated by changing a local preference.

The earlier interface `openTradeChat(binding, participants, relayIds, signal)`, `subscribe(cursor)` and the queued/sent/acknowledged/received delivery states belong to the relay layer and are deferred.
The limits of four relay connections and 500 events per batch still apply there.
Results use the shared G13 `CoreResult` and `createCoreError`, with a fresh correlation id and no content, key or relay data:
| Code | Cause |
| `INVALID_INPUT` | Malformed binding, keys, options, event or clock. |
| `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | Content, rumor JSON, tag count, payload size, or the seen-set bound. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` | Kind 4 at any layer, or an unknown NIP-44 version. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER` | The provider lacks sign, ECDH or generate. |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | Not addressed to self, a seal/rumor author mismatch, a non-participant, wrong binding tags, or a secret that does not match the session key. |
| `INTEGRITY_FAILURE` | Bad id, signature or MAC. |
| `LOCKED` / `CANCELLED` | The session is closed, or the signal was aborted. |
There is no retry, and no fallback to NIP-04 or to unwrapped kind-14 events.
Chat messages never propose economic effects; operations that do pass core preflight, durable G12 reservation and fresh external-wallet consent, which this module cannot bypass.
Gift wrapping reduces exposed social graph but relay subscriptions, IP, timing, retained ciphertext and endpoint compromise remain.
Encryption cannot make public order discovery confidential.
Expiry/deletion cannot erase relay copies.
| Attack | Mitigation |
| Impersonation: a third party wraps a rumor claiming a counterparty's key | `seal.pubkey == rumor.pubkey`, and the seal signature is verified. |
| An outsider who knows the trade injects messages | The author must be one of the two participants taken from terms. |
| Cross-trade or cross-conversation replay between the same two people | Exact `trade` and `conversation` tags. The conversation id commits to chain, network, deployment, tradeId and both keys. |
| Redirect: a wrap addressed to someone else, or several `p` tags | Exactly one `p` tag, naming self. |
| Relay duplicates or re-wraps | Rumor-id deduplication. The bound is refused, never evicted. |
| Timestamp correlation | Seal and wrap times are uniform over 2 days. Wrap keys are fresh per wrap. Wrap times are not used for ordering. |
| Downgrade to NIP-04, or plaintext kind 14 | Kind 4 is rejected at every layer. Only kind 1059 is accepted on the outer layer. |
| Seal metadata leak | Seal tags MUST be empty and are enforced on both build and receive. |
| Hostile objects and oversized relay input | Strict parsers. Bounds run before signature work and decryption. Errors are redacted. |
| Late plaintext after lock | Close and abort are re-checked after every await. |
Residual limits:
- Bare `createTradeChat` deduplication is per session and in memory.
Consumers using the optional G02 durable composition retain replay memory across reload/restore; consumers of the bare core must provide that persistence themselves.
- Each counterparty sees the other's long-term messaging key.
A compromised messaging key decrypts all past and future messages (no forward secrecy).
- The self copy reveals to the sender's relays that the sender received a wrap.
- `claimedCreatedAt` can be any value the sender chooses.
- One-time secrets are wiped from their byte arrays, but noble's internal bigints and JavaScript strings cannot be wiped.

The system authority contract governs this module: external wallets authorize spending; deployed escrow and reconciled chain observations establish custody state; relay and local data are untrusted claims.
This specification creates no operator release path, automatic bank payment or authority over an already funded trade.
Missing optional infrastructure MUST preserve basic release/refund and encrypted recovery paths.
Public localStorage may contain only non-sensitive UI theme and a versioned last-used opaque profile locator.
Identity, trade IDs, chat, notes, PINs, passphrases and journal content belong in encrypted G02 records.
Browser storage persistence is not durability.
Runtime validation MUST reject unknown versions/properties, unsafe integers, duplicate identities and oversized inputs before expensive work.
Network, deployment, trade and account generation are explicit bindings where economic state is involved.
Amounts are unsigned decimal base-unit strings, never floating point.
Immutable results and defensive copies prevent consumers mutating validated state.
Protocol-specific limits override broader application limits.
On startup validate public hints and ignore malformed/stale values without deleting vaults.
Start locked; reconcile encrypted records only after unlock.
Lock on page hide and five minutes without trusted keyboard/pointer activity per G02; polling does not extend idle.
Explicit local profile deletion requires authenticated user confirmation and backup warning, separately from routine recovery; it never implies physical erasure.
Asynchronous jobs carry a generation and AbortSignal.
Revoked generations MUST NOT publish late plaintext, restore stale coverage or initiate new economic work.
Dispose removes subscriptions and closes owned resources.
Cancellation after broadcast is an uncertain transaction outcome requiring journal reconciliation, not proof of rollback.
Existing signed/funded terms cannot be renegotiated by changing a local preference.
loadPublicHints(), saveTheme(theme), lockAll() and requestProfileRemoval(profileId, consent) have bounded schemas.
Database upgrade/versionchange invalidates sessions.
Quota or unavailable storage returns typed errors and preserves the last complete snapshot.
All interfaces return the shared core result/error contract.

Distinguish INVALID_INPUT, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER, UNAUTHORIZED, LOCKED, CANCELLED and unavailable external service; map concrete errors to registered G13 codes without exposing private content.
No unbounded retry, secret-bearing diagnostics, destructive reset or silent downgrade is permitted.
Operations that propose economic effects pass core preflight, durable G12 reservation and fresh external-wallet consent; this module cannot bypass them.
Eviction, origin changes, backups, browser sync and OS snapshots can retain or remove data.
IndexedDB deletion cannot wipe SSD remnants or relay/chain history.
Service-worker caches must not contain private API payloads.
Active origin compromise, malicious extensions and a compromised OS can read unlocked state; capability wrappers are not a same-origin JavaScript sandbox.
Transport encryption, payload encryption and chain privacy are independent properties.
G02 remains the exact v1 storage authority: no alternative KDF, AAD, record kind or session token is introduced here.
G03 alone governs authenticated fresh-key restore.
No physical erasure, global anonymity or provider availability guarantee is made.
Test storage denied, quota, eviction, CID-origin change, pagehide, idle timer spoofing, corrupt hints and profile removal cancellation.
No error handler may clear the database automatically.

Export portable encrypted local state and restore it without overwriting a healthy vault or reusing a prior DEK write budget.
Preserve G02's exact authenticated envelope.
A backup does not contain external-wallet spending keys and does not make relay history or chain observations authoritative.

The canonical envelope has exact G02 field order: format, version, profileId, keyId, revision, wrappedKey, snapshot. wrappedKey order is kdf, iterations, salt, cipher, nonce, ciphertext; snapshot order is nonce, ciphertext.
Serialize without whitespace using UTF-8 JSON.
Checksum detects accidental transport corruption only; AES-GCM authentication decides authenticity.
Exports MUST state whether the current envelope was authenticated in this session.
Exporting a locked envelope is permitted by G02 but is not a verified recovery test.
Export reads one complete committed G02 envelope, validates its public bounds, canonicalizes it, computes SHA-256, and emits one BackupV1 JSON file.
Never include filenames, account addresses, private record summaries, or passphrases in the envelope header.
Import caps input at 12 MiB before parsing; G02 ciphertext's base64 expansion fits this bound.
Reject duplicate JSON keys, unknown fields, noncanonical base64url, unsupported version/KDF/count, non-safe revision, wrong lengths, or checksum mismatch before any expensive KDF.
Streaming input must stop at the limit.
Authenticate and decrypt the source using G02's exact PBKDF2-SHA256 600000-iteration, AES-256-GCM, padding, AAD, record count, and payload limits.
Check all duplicated metadata.
No partial records become visible on any failure.
Create independent random destination profile ID, key ID, 32-byte DEK, 32-byte salt, and 12-byte nonces.
Derive a new KEK from the destination passphrase with G02's unchanged profile.
Destination passphrase may equal source passphrase but salt and DEK MUST be fresh.
Reset revision to 0 and re-encrypt the complete validated snapshot with destination metadata.
Preserve record IDs and payload bytes; record consumers MUST validate their own schemas after restore.
Trade chain/deployment IDs remain original.
Do not silently relabel a chain or rewrite an identity key.
Old-profile-specific records require an explicit consumer migration before use.
Perform a final destination envelope round-trip authentication before storage.
Use one IndexedDB `add` transaction; report success only after transaction completion.
A profile collision fails without retrying a `put`.
The old vault is never deleted or overwritten.
Select the new profile in UI only after success; there is no persistent active-profile pointer in v1, so startup presents profile selection.
Restored source data is never opened as writable with its old DEK.
Source decryption occurs in a temporary recovery context, which is discarded on completion/cancel.
At most one recovery job per document runs.
No Web Crypto await occurs inside an active IDB transaction.
The checksum is unkeyed and adds no protection against intentional modification.
Source freshness/rollback cannot be proven from an offline backup.
Public BackupService.restore is byte-preserving and accepts no transform or executable migration input.
Bundled G09 migrations use a separate storage-internal interface:

This service revalidates the live source session/key/revision, resolves only a bundled registered deterministic transform, validates every source/destination record and G02 aggregate bounds, then generates fresh destination keys and uses the same authenticate-before-add atomic destination pipeline.

Recheck source revision immediately before the destination transaction; include the source row in that read-write transaction and abort if it changed, so a concurrent commit cannot make the new profile silently omit work.
The source profile is retained.
This internal migration may change registered record payload schemas; it is not exposed to backup imports and does not weaken ordinary restore's byte-preservation rule.
Return typed G02 errors plus `CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` and `BUSY`.
Wrong passphrase, failed GCM authentication, and malformed authenticated plaintext all become `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` with no inner details.
A syntactically invalid public envelope returns `INVALID_INPUT` or `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` before derivation.
User cancellation before storage starts has no durable effect; during transaction request abort and wait for terminal outcome.
If commit wins, return the receipt.
After an uncertain storage failure list/reconcile profile IDs before retry.
Do not automatically delete apparently duplicate restored profiles.
UI shows source age as untrusted information and reconciles every pending trade on-chain before permitting economic actions.
A malicious backup can trigger excessive allocation/KDF work: enforce encoded and decoded bounds first and allow one worker/job.
Reusing source keys can exceed nonce budgets: fresh-key restore is mandatory.
Tampered metadata and ciphertext fail authenticated decryption.
A checksum-recomputed malicious envelope still fails GCM unless attacker knows the passphrase; a malicious producer who does know it can forge contents, so backups are not third-party evidence.
Downloads, clipboard, browser extensions, and unlocked memory expose data outside the vault's control.
Cross-origin restore is explicit file import only; no hidden iframe/key sharing or automatic gateway migration.
Device loss without a usable backup may permanently lose messaging/history data.
Test fresh-origin and same-origin restore; verify identical record bytes, fresh profile/key/salt/nonces, revision zero, and intact old vault.
Test 12 MiB boundary, truncated JSON/ciphertext, duplicate keys, unknown nested fields, invalid canonical encoding, excessive KDF count, bad checksum, wrong password, swapped fields and wrong AAD.
Spy KDF to ensure public-invalid files perform zero derivations.
Inject crash/cancel/quota/collision before and during commit; reopening must reveal complete old and/or complete new profiles only.
Verify restoring the same backup twice uses unrelated keys, and subsequent writes do not reuse the imported DEK.
Run Web Crypto and independent implementation fixtures.
Real-browser IndexedDB evidence is required before recovery is supported.

Store private application records in an authenticated encrypted IndexedDB vault.
Prevent an offline reader of browser storage from reading record contents without the passphrase, and reject modified ciphertext before parsing private data.
Version 1 deliberately encrypts one bounded snapshot per profile rather than one independent ciphertext per business record.
Records are a typed collection inside that snapshot.
This avoids partial-record migration and cross-record consistency problems during the MVP; the cost is rewriting at most 8 MiB per update.
Large attachments, maps, bank transcripts, and bulk chat archives do not belong in this vault.
A later sharded format requires a distinct reviewed version.
The vault stores messaging key material only where required by the selected signer model, preferences, encrypted chat records, and transaction recovery references.
It MUST NOT store wallet spending seeds/private keys, bank login credentials, or unbounded prover witnesses.
A connected external signer may eliminate local messaging-secret storage.
Threat coverage is confidentiality at rest and detection of unauthenticated modification.

It does not prevent a malicious active origin from reading unlocked data, a wallet extension from disclosing data, browser eviction, deletion, rollback to a complete authentic historical vault, or compromise of the passphrase.
The offline passphrase-guessing risk remains material.
No physical secure-deletion guarantee is made.

requirements.text:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as UI
    participant V as Vault service
    participant C as Web Crypto
    participant D as IndexedDB
    U->>V: unlock(profileId, passphrase)
    V->>D: Read one bounded envelope
    D-->>V: Ciphertext and metadata
    V->>C: Derive KEK and authenticate wrapped DEK
    V->>C: Decrypt snapshot with bound metadata
    V-->>U: Session handle and revision
    U->>V: Commit batch with expected revision
    V->>C: Encrypt new snapshot outside IDB transaction
    V->>D: Compare revision and replace row atomically
    D-->>V: Transaction complete or conflict
    V-->>U: Committed revision or typed error
```
The TypeScript declarations specify the wire/storage shape; runtime validation is mandatory.
Strings use strict canonical unpadded base64url or lowercase hex where stated.
Implementations MUST reject unknown properties at every object level and MUST not coerce values.
`profileId`, `keyId`, and record IDs match `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`.
Base64url matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`, has no padding, decodes within bounds, and MUST re-encode identically; this rejects ambiguous trailing bits.
Numbers are finite safe integers with the bounds above.
Reject duplicate IDs, unknown kinds, malformed JSON, extra fields, and unsupported versions.
A zero-length payload is allowed at storage level but may be rejected by its consumer.
Serialize the private snapshot as UTF-8 JSON with the property order shown in the type definitions, no optional properties, and records sorted lexicographically by ID.
No user text is interpolated into metadata encodings.
Consumers serialize their own payload bytes and validate them after read.
The storage service returns defensive copies, never mutable aliases into the cached snapshot.
Let `J` be those JSON bytes and `L = len(J)`.
Require `L <= 8_388_604` and encode plaintext as `u32be(L) || J || zeroPadding`, padded to a multiple of 4096 bytes with total length at most 8_388_608.
After authentication, check the length prefix, maximum bound, zero padding, UTF-8 validity, and exact snapshot schema.
Padding reduces length granularity; it does not conceal growth or update timing.
Ciphertext decoded size MUST be a multiple of 4096 plus 16 and between 4112 and 8_388_624 bytes.
All randomness comes from `crypto.getRandomValues`.
Creation generates independent random DEK (32 bytes), KDF salt (32 bytes), profile ID (16 bytes), key ID (16 bytes), wrapping nonce (12 bytes), and snapshot nonce (12 bytes).
Reject passphrases containing unpaired UTF-16 surrogates.
Encode the exact entered string as UTF-8 with no trimming, case conversion, or Unicode normalization.
Creation and unlocking accept 12..1024 UTF-8 bytes; the UI encourages a password-manager-generated secret or strong multiword passphrase and never describes length alone as entropy.
Rate-limit UI attempts for usability and resource protection, while explicitly acknowledging this does not stop offline guessing.
The v1 interoperable browser profile is:
`KEK = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(UTF8(passphrase), salt, 600000, 32 bytes)`
`wrappedDEK = AES-256-GCM(KEK, wrapNonce, rawDEK, AAD_wrap, tagLength=128)`
`snapshotCiphertext = AES-256-GCM(DEK, snapshotNonce, paddedSnapshot, AAD_snapshot, tagLength=128)`
This is a project design choice favoring browser-native Web Crypto for the initial profile, not a claim that PBKDF2 is memory-hard or the strongest password KDF.
Argon2id would require an independently reviewed, versioned profile and implementation.
Never silently lower the iteration count on a slow device.
Reject other KDF names/counts before doing expensive work; a new profile requires a format migration.
Define `E(array) = UTF8(JSON.stringify(array))` over the ordered arrays below; entries are ASCII literals, canonical encoded IDs/salt, and bounded integers:

```text
AAD_wrap = E(["p2p-offramp", "vault-key", 1, profileId, keyId,
              "PBKDF2-SHA256", 600000, salt])
AAD_snapshot = E(["p2p-offramp", "vault-snapshot", 1,
                  profileId, keyId, revision])
```
Encryption uses Web Crypto `AES-GCM`, 96-bit IVs and 128-bit tags.
The API ciphertext representation is ciphertext followed by authentication tag.
Salt is not reused for a newly created vault.
Each new snapshot encryption MUST use an independently random nonce; never derive it solely from revision, because imported backups can roll revisions backward.
For `q` independent random snapshot nonces under one DEK, the birthday collision upper bound is `q(q-1)/2^97`; at an illustrative `q = 2^20` it is below `2^-57`.

The revision limit does **not** enforce that cryptographic invocation bound: pre-CAS encryption on conflicts, cancellation or quota failures consumes random nonces without a committed revision, and other tabs/reopened sessions also use the key.
Do not advertise an enforced lifetime `q <= 2^20` guarantee.
Core v1 accepts random-96-bit-IV risk under this explicitly bounded operational policy, subject to independent cryptographic review before enabling private production storage.
Initial creation uses revision 0; committing from revision 1_048_575 returns `REKEY_REQUIRED` before encryption.

Additionally each unlocked key material handle counts every attempted snapshot encryption before invoking Web Crypto, including discarded failures; at 4096 attempts it refuses further encryption with `REKEY_REQUIRED` until fresh-key migration.
No automatic retry of failed writes is allowed.
This per-handle counter does not survive process loss and is not a global multi-tab invocation bound; that residual limit must appear in the security review.
A future globally enforced budget requires a separately reviewed durable reservation/format design, not a misleading reinterpretation of revision.
Rekeying uses authenticated G03/G09 fresh-key export/import or internal migration, generating a fresh DEK/key ID and resetting revision; copying an old envelope does not qualify.
Restored source data is not writable until imported under fresh keys.
G03 owns ordinary restore and the strictly bundled internal migration/reseal operation; v1 direct same-profile overwrite/import is not exposed by VaultService.
Unwrap the DEK only after validating envelope bounds.
Import the unwrapped raw bytes as a non-extractable AES-GCM `CryptoKey` with encrypt/decrypt usage, then overwrite reachable temporary byte arrays where possible.
Creation generates raw random DEK bytes, encrypts them under KEK, imports them, and drops raw references.
Never persist a plaintext `CryptoKey` or password.
This does not make JavaScript memory reliably zeroizable.
No Poseidon, secp256k1, ZK circuit, or on-chain contract is needed for this component.
Serialize calls within one session; reject batches over 256 mutations or duplicate mutation IDs.
Require an unlocked session and matching `expectedRevision`.
Read the latest envelope in a short read-only transaction.
Check profile/key/revision match the cached authenticated snapshot.
If they differ, return `CONFLICT` and require a fresh unlock; do not overwrite changes from another tab.
Apply mutations to a copy, increment revision once, validate all limits, encode and encrypt with a fresh nonce outside an IndexedDB write transaction.
Deleting a nonexistent record is an idempotent mutation; an empty batch returns the current revision without a write.

Open one read-write transaction for `vaults`, reread the row, compare key ID and revision to the originally read row, then replace the entire envelope while preserving the unchanged wrapped-key object.
Abort on mismatch.
IndexedDB serialization of overlapping read-write transactions supplies atomic compare-and-swap across tabs.
Publish the new cached snapshot/revision and success only on transaction completion, never on an individual request's success.
Abort/error leaves the old committed envelope intact.
A quota failure returns `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` and keeps the old cached revision.

Every read-write transaction (`add`, compare-and-swap, reseal `add` with source recheck) requests `durability: 'strict'`: under the IndexedDB 'default' hint a user agent may report completion before the write is flushed, and a later OS crash or power loss could roll back a revision already reported and acted on (for example the G12 `broadcast-unknown` marker that must be durable before any wallet send).
Engines without the option ignore it; that residual is part of the security review.
Do not await Web Crypto inside an open IndexedDB transaction: it may become inactive before the asynchronous operation finishes.
Database upgrades and `versionchange` events close the connection and invalidate sessions.
Unsupported future DB versions return `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`; never delete a database as automatic recovery.
`create` validates the passphrase, generates an empty encrypted snapshot at revision 0, and uses `add`, not `put`, so a random-ID collision cannot overwrite data.
Return `ALREADY_EXISTS` on collision.
Creation succeeds only after transaction completion and returns one unlocked session.
`unlock` bounds-checks, derives KEK, unwraps DEK, decrypts and validates the snapshot, checks all duplicated profile/key/revision fields, then creates a random session token.
Wrong passwords, tag failures, and invalid decrypted content return the same `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` public error without exposing a parsing oracle.
Unsupported public format and invalid outer bounds are rejected before derivation.
Never return partial plaintext.
`read` and `list` operate on authenticated cached data and return copies; they do not assert that the cache is the newest version.
`commit` is the synchronization point.
Another tab's modification produces `CONFLICT`, not silent merge.
A UI using a cached trade record MUST reconcile actual escrow state with the chain before any economic action.
`lock` marks a session unusable immediately, increments its in-memory generation token, and drops cached plaintext/key references.
Every asynchronous operation checks that token before publishing plaintext or starting a write transaction.
If a write transaction is already active, attempt abort; if it already committed, data remains encrypted and the promise resolves with the committed revision.
`lockAll` also fires on page hide; idle lock occurs after five minutes without trusted keyboard/pointer activity.
Read/list polling MUST NOT reset that idle timer.
These controls apply per document; browser-wide coordinated locking may signal other tabs but cannot guarantee they obey.
Cancellation before a write transaction returns `CANCELLED`; during an active transaction, request abort and wait for the terminal outcome.
If commit wins, return the committed revision, not a false cancellation.
An uncertain storage failure requires rereading/unlocking to discover the persisted revision before retrying.
Web Crypto operations may finish after cancellation; their outputs are discarded if the session generation changed.
`exportEncrypted` returns an immutable copy of the current bounded envelope and contains no plaintext.
Authentication and safe fresh-key restore belong to G03.
Passphrase changes are not in-place operations in v1: use authenticated fresh-key migration.
The service exposes no API to delete an entire vault during routine error recovery.
`UNSUPPORTED_ENVIRONMENT` covers missing secure context, Web Crypto, or IndexedDB.
`NOT_FOUND` requires explicit user action; do not silently create an empty replacement.
`LIMIT_EXCEEDED` requests archive/export before retry.
`REKEY_REQUIRED` requests a fresh-key migration.
`CONFLICT` requires reload/unlock; `LOCKED` requires unlock.
Authentication/format/input errors are non-retryable without changed input.
Storage availability and quota errors may be retried after user remediation, never in an unbounded loop.
Diagnostic messages are fixed strings and do not include profile contents, passphrases, payload bytes, or external errors containing secrets.
| Attack or failure | Required mitigation and remaining limit |
| Offline database theft | Password-wrapped random DEK and authenticated snapshot; weak passphrases still permit guessing |
| Ciphertext/header substitution | GCM authentication binds profile, key, and revision; decrypted duplicate metadata must match |
| Historical snapshot replay | Current authenticated revision prevents ordinary accidental mixing; complete authentic vault rollback cannot be detected without an external trusted freshness anchor |
| Nonce reuse after restore | Random nonces, committed-revision/per-handle attempt limits, fresh-key restore; no claimed global attempt cap or counter-only nonce design |
| Malicious origin/XSS/dependency | CSP, inert rendering, reviewed dependencies, and minimal secret lifetime; active origin compromise defeats unlocked confidentiality |
| Concurrent tabs | Read-write transactional revision compare-and-swap; conflicts force reload rather than overwriting |
| Malformed envelope DoS | Strict encoded/decoded bounds and exact KDF parameters before derivation; one unlock attempt at a time per document |
| Quota, eviction, device loss | Fail without destructive reset and require encrypted backup; persistence permission is not a durability guarantee |
| Metadata leakage | Opaque IDs, encrypted record metadata, 4096-byte padding; profile count, size buckets, and activity remain observable |
| Changed IPFS origin | Explicit backup/restore; never assume IndexedDB crosses gateway/CID origin boundaries |
| Wallet or chain-state confusion | Spending keys remain external; vault records are recovery hints, not chain authority |
Two applications on the same compromised origin are not isolated by this module.
Origin deployment policy is a separate prerequisite.
Browser developer tools, crash dumps, OS compromise, screenshots, and hostile extensions are outside the at-rest guarantee.
Run PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and AES-GCM vectors from independently verified fixtures, including empty plaintext for primitive tests and a 128-bit tag.
Compare browser output with an independent implementation, using injected deterministic randomness only in tests.
Round-trip an empty vault, all five record kinds, maximum payload, maximum snapshot size, Unicode passphrases, and canonical base64url.
Verify unpaired surrogate and out-of-range inputs reject.
Flip each public bound metadata field and representative ciphertext/tag bits.
Require rejection without plaintext.
Wrong password and authenticated-content parsing failure share the same external error code.
Substitute profile/key/revision across envelopes and reject; replay a complete authentic historical envelope and verify the documented limitation rather than asserting anti-rollback protection.
Exercise duplicate record IDs, duplicate mutations, unknown properties, illegal kinds, unsafe numbers, nonzero padding, and malformed UTF-8.
Verify revision cap: last allowed commit succeeds; next returns `REKEY_REQUIRED` without creating ciphertext or modifying storage.
Test repeated failed encryptions from conflicts/quota/cancel: attempted encryptions increment the per-handle counter even if revision is unchanged, and attempt 4097 refuses before Web Crypto.
Test two independent tabs and reopened sessions explicitly to demonstrate that the revision and per-handle counters do not enforce a global nonce invocation bound.
Run two real browser tabs committing from the same revision: exactly one succeeds and one conflicts.
Inject failure before encryption, after encryption, before write, during request processing, on abort, and after transaction completion.
Restart the page and assert that either the complete old or complete new authenticated envelope exists, never a partially updated row.
Run quota denial, storage disabled, database upgrade blocking, versionchange, and origin-change restore scenarios.
Lock/cancel during KDF, decryption, encryption, and commit.
No plaintext result may escape a revoked session.
If a transaction committed before locking, its durable revision must be discoverable on unlock.
Do not assert immediate physical erasure of buffers.
Use 10,000 generated malformed-envelope cases per deterministic seed and 100,000 bounded random mutation sequences in scheduled testing.
Generate 0..256 mutations per batch, 0..10,000 records, and payload boundaries at 0, 1, 262143, 262144, and 262145 decoded bytes.
Exercise snapshot lengths around each 4096-byte boundary and the 8 MiB ceiling.
Oversized/KDF-invalid envelopes must be rejected before a KDF spy records a call.

Measure unlock latency and peak memory on each supported desktop/mobile browser using the fixed KDF profile; publish p50/p95 results with device identifiers and runtime versions before enabling that browser.
Resource failures must leave the old vault usable and return a typed error.
Do not weaken the KDF to meet a performance target.
ZK proof verification tests are not applicable because this module emits no ZK proof.
Acceptance requires successful interoperability, real IndexedDB concurrency tests, corruption/failure cases, and a recorded security review of the concrete implementation.
Passing this specification's tests is evidence for these properties, not proof that the entire application is secure.
- [Web Cryptography API Recommendation](https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-WebCryptoAPI-20170126/): browser primitive operations; v1 uses established AES-GCM/PBKDF2 operations.
